timing: After baseline_attempt1 stopped before loading the first checkpoint tensor and before any direct baseline output, endpoint, internal state, or mechanism estimate was produced.
diagnosis: The direct loader passed a source-lock checkpoint reference augmented with tensor_hashes to the legacy training-strategy verifier. That verifier compares the complete dictionary against a three-field materialized reference, so it rejected the additional metadata even though path, byte count, SHA-256, and on-disk bytes were identical.

repair.reference_verifier: The direct loader must use this successor's materialized-reference verifier, which validates path, bytes, and SHA-256 while allowing separately locked tensor_hashes metadata; after deserialization it must continue to verify every model tensor against tensor_hashes.
repair.qualification: Write a new qualification_v2.json covering the changed source. The original qualification remains immutable.
repair.source_lock: Write a new baseline_source_lock_v2.json from a clean implementation commit. The original source lock remains immutable and belongs to baseline_attempt1.
repair.execution_status: Because attempt1 completed zero units and exposed no direct model output, the repaired command is the first Phase-1 scientific baseline execution, not a replay of an observed baseline. Preserve attempt1 as a noninterpretable method attempt.

unchanged: all checkpoints, tensor identities, seeds, panels, conditions, cells, and frozen inputs
the one eager float32 32D direct arithmetic authority and all deterministic runtime settings
same-process bitwise replay, external array tolerances, parent classification compatibility, and stop rules
all Stage 1--3 estimands, interventions, probes, statistics, thresholds, labels, and claim boundaries
the prohibition on training, adapter internal-state comparison, and mechanism execution before a compatible frozen baseline
